claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.

experiment_recipes.goal: Check if a parameter-based editor already achieves reliable, locality-preserving single edits without capability loss (a quick potential refutation of the claim).
metrics: Score S (harmonic mean of ES, PS, NS)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Proceed (claim not refuted) if MEMIT fails to meet ALL of the following on single-edit evaluation over the standard COUNTERFACT split: ES >= 0.95, PS >= 0.95, NS >= 0.98, Score S >= 0.95, Locality >= 0.98, ΔME-PPL ≤ 10% vs pre-edit, and ΔMMLU ≤ 1.0 point. If ALL thresholds are satisfied, refute the claim and stop.
constraints_not_enforced: Cross-model/backbone replication not performed in this gate
experiment_recipes.rationale: If a canonical parameter-based editor achieves near-perfect edit quality with negligible locality/capability cost under the standard COUNTERFACT suite, the claim is directly contradicted; this is the cheapest decisive check.

experiment_recipes.goal: Build and validate a representation-geometry apparatus (PC subspaces at edit-relevant layers/tokens) to quantify low-variance alignment of edits.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Validate apparatus if: (i) The Pearson correlation of per-layer explained-variance spectra between two random half-splits of COUNTERFACT prompts is ρ ≥ 0.95 with p < 1e-6; and (ii) Across 5 bootstrap resamples, the mean pairwise correlation of the top-64 PC score vectors at the peak edit layer (by tracing) is ρ ≥ 0.90 (95% CI lower bound ≥ 0.85). Failure to meet either threshold invalidates the geometry apparatus.
constraints_not_enforced: Absolute explained-variance thresholds not enforced due to metric menu; stability used instead
No cross-dataset geometry validation in this step
experiment_recipes.rationale: The claim’s geometric mechanism requires a stable notion of low-variance directions. This step constructs and validates those subspaces so later headline tests can measure alignment and amplification meaningfully.

experiment_recipes.goal: Test whether near-perfect single-edit results survive realistic evaluation and whether reliability is attainable without capability damage under sequential edits.
metrics: Score S (harmonic mean of ES, PS, NS)
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Support the claim if BOTH of the following hold: (A) Near-perfect single-edit does not hold: Score S < 0.95 OR PS < 0.95 on the full COUNTERFACT eval split; AND (B) Under n = 100 cumulative sequential edits (no rollback), at least one capability/locality damage criterion is triggered: Locality < 0.95 OR ΔME-PPL > 20% vs pre-edit OR ΔMMLU > 2.0 points OR Prob.Drop > 0.5 on ≥ 10% of probed original facts OR ForgettingRate ≥ 10%. If neither (A) nor (B) is triggered, refute the claim.
constraints_not_enforced: Multi-hop MQuAKE evaluation not included in this step
depends_on: Check if a parameter-based editor already achieves reliable, locality-preserving single edits without capability loss (a quick potential refutation of the claim).
experiment_recipes.rationale: The claim centers on realistic evaluation and sequential retention. This protocol exercises paraphrase/neighborhood, portability, and cumulative-edit stability with out-of-scope locality and unrelated-task health checks.

experiment_recipes.goal: Test geometric limitation: low-variance alignment of edit updates predicts locality/capability damage beyond layer choice.
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Statistical modeling of localization vs outcomes
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Support the geometric mechanism if: (i) Across edits, the alignment of the edit-induced parameter delta with the bottom-quartile PC variance subspace at the chosen edit layer correlates with Locality drop (or ForgettingRate increase) with ρ ≥ 0.50 and p < 0.01; AND (ii) A regression predicting Locality drop from [layer (categorical) + low-variance alignment] increases R^2 by ≥ 0.15 over a layer-only model with an F-test p < 0.01. If either (i) or (ii) fails, this part of the claim is not supported.
constraints_not_enforced: Causal-path mediation (MLP vs attention) not tested here
depends_on: Build and validate a representation-geometry apparatus (PC subspaces at edit-relevant layers/tokens) to quantify low-variance alignment of edits.
experiment_recipes.rationale: The claim asserts a geometric, not incidental, limitation. This tests whether low-variance alignment explains damage beyond the confound of edit-layer selection.

experiment_recipes.goal: Directly test amplification: equal-norm updates along low-variance vs high-variance subspaces cause disproportionate off-target change.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Support the amplification claim if, at the same Frobenius norm of the applied update and at the same layer: (a) Low-variance–subspace-targeted updates produce ≥ 2× larger Locality drop than high-variance–subspace-targeted updates on O(x,y); AND (b) Low-variance updates increase ME-PPL and/or Prob.Drop by ≥ 2× relative to high-variance updates; AND (c) CKA FalseRate is higher for low-variance than high-variance updates by ≥ 25% relative. Failure of any sub-condition refutes amplification.
constraints_not_enforced: Exact equality of functional effect on the edited fact is not enforced (we hold parameter-norm equal rather than effect-equal)
depends_on: Build and validate a representation-geometry apparatus (PC subspaces at edit-relevant layers/tokens) to quantify low-variance alignment of edits.
experiment_recipes.rationale: To establish a geometric limitation, a controlled intervention must show that equal-norm moves along low-variance directions yield disproportionately large off-target changes compared to high-variance directions.

experiment_recipes.goal: Isolate that the observed instability is specific to parameter-based editing by comparing to parameter-preserving editors under identical evaluation.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Support parameter-specificity if, at n = 100 sequential edits on the same instances as MEMIT in the headline: SERAC achieves Reliability ≥ 0.90, Locality ≥ 0.98, ΔME-PPL ≤ 10%, and ΔMMLU ≤ 1.0 point, while MEMIT (from the headline run) violates at least one of these thresholds. If SERAC also violates the thresholds to a similar extent (within 10% relative), the result does not isolate parameter-based editing as the cause and weakens the claim.
depends_on: Test whether near-perfect single-edit results survive realistic evaluation and whether reliability is attainable without capability damage under sequential edits.
experiment_recipes.rationale: If non-parameter editors retain locality/capabilities where parameter-based methods fail, the degradation is attributable to modifying base weights rather than the act of editing per se.
